title: SIU clears OPP officer in disabled man's death
subtitle: The neighbour of a developmentally delayed man gunned down by an OPP constable in June says she is "upset" that the Special Investigations Unit cleared the unnamed officer of any wrongdoing on Wednesday.
article: The neighbour of a developmentally delayed man gunned down by an OPP constable in June says she is "upset" that the Special Investigations Unit cleared the unnamed officer of any wrongdoing on Wednesday.
"It's not what we expected; it's not what should have happened," said Marguerite Stone of Elmvale, Ont., northwest of Barrie.

Douglas Minty, 59, was shot multiple times and killed on June 22, at the foot of the driveway of his bungalow. The OPP officer had been dispatched following a dispute between Minty and a salesman. The SIU said the officer approached Minty, who advanced with a knife in his hand. Then, instead of dropping the knife, as ordered, he charged threateningly and was shot, the probe determined.
But Stone, who saw the episode some 10 metres from Minty's driveway, says, "There was no sign of him attacking with a knife."
Seven SIU investigators, including three forensic specialists, looked into the incident.
